result.summary:
Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md and docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md exactly as designed -- the T+2h post-event feedback request with a single T+24h reminder, NPS/liked/improve/topicVotes, and the once-only broadcast-opt-in ask.

1. Schema (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts, migration generated via `npx drizzle-kit generate`, never hand-written, per decisions/0005): new `feedback` table -- registrationId (uuid NOT NULL, UNIQUE index uq_feedback_registration_id, FK -> registrations.id ON DELETE restrict), nps (integer NOT NULL, CHECK chk_feedback_nps_range 0-10), liked/improve (nullable text), topicVotes (text[], nullable), likedSkipped/improveSkipped/topicVotesSkipped (boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false), createdAt/updatedAt. New users.broadcastOptInAskedAt (nullable timestamptz, placed immediately after broadcastOptIn). Generated migration apps/bot/drizzle/0006_smiling_leader.sql matches REQ-031-schema.md Sec6's expected statement shape exactly (CREATE TABLE feedback, ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN, the FK, the unique index -- no other statement). Re-running `drizzle-kit generate` after writing the schema.ts edits reported 'No schema changes, nothing to migrate', confirming schema.ts and the already-generated migration stay in lockstep.

2. apps/bot/src/domain/feedback.ts (NEW): FEEDBACK_FIELD_ORDER/FeedbackField (Sec2.1), getFeedbackByRegistrationId/determineNextFeedbackField/isFeedbackComplete (Sec2.2's exact first-match-wins table), isValidNpsValue/writeFeedbackNps (Sec2.3 -- the sole INSERT path, ON CONFLICT (registration_id) DO UPDATE, matching the design's stated re-answer allowance), writeFeedbackOptionalField/markFeedbackFieldSkipped (Sec2.4 -- UPDATE only, never INSERT, reachable only once a row exists), determineFeedbackFlowStep (Sec2.7 -- layers the broadcast-ask on top of the field progression, gated on broadcastOptInAskedAt !== null per AC5, never on the boolean answer value), FEEDBACK_REF_LINE_PREFIX/FEEDBACK_FIELD_LINE_PREFIX/formatFeedbackTextPrompt/parseFeedbackReplyContext (Sec3.1's exact two-line disambiguation pattern -- 'Feedback ref: '/'Feedback field: ', mirroring domain/walkin.ts's own 'Name: '/'Company: '/'Phone: ' exact-prefix convention), parseTopicVotes (Sec3.4 -- split on newline/comma, trim, drop empty, no de-dup), isFeedbackSkipReply (Sec4).

3. apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (extended): added getRegistrationFeedbackContext (Sec2.5 -- a new function, not a reshape of getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent, per the design's own reasoning) returning userId/eventId/admission/checkedInAt -- checkedInAt is what makes AC1 checkable both at write time here and in the scheduler's own selection queries.

4. apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts (extended): added getUserFeedbackStateById and writeBroadcastOptInAnswer (Sec2.6) -- the latter is the ONLY function anywhere in this codebase that writes users.broadcast_opt_in or users.broadcast_opt_in_asked_at, both columns written by the same UPDATE statement, always together, mirroring consentPdAt/consentPdVersion's existing pairing discipline.

5. apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts: NotificationKind gained 'feedback_reminder' (Sec5.1) -- a one-line TypeScript change, no migration ('feedback_request' already existed in the union, added defensively ahead of this requirement).

6. apps/bot/src/scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts (NEW): selectRegistrationsForFeedbackRequest/selectRegistrationsForFeedbackReminder (Sec5.2/5.3 -- checked_in_at IS NOT NULL is AC1's entire mechanism; the reminder query additionally excludes any registration with an existing feedback row via a NOT IN subquery, Sec5.3's own named 'did they engage' reading; both use a bounded CATCH_UP_WINDOW_MS of 2 hours, Sec10 open question 3, sized as a generous multiple -- 24x -- of the 5-minute polling interval), makeFeedbackRequestJob/makeFeedbackReminderJob (Sec5.4/5.5 -- both send via sendLedgeredNotification with classification:'transactional' [AC7] and their own distinct NotificationKind [AC4's entire double-send-prevention mechanism, via REQ-025's UNIQUE(registration_id,kind) ledger constraint]; composeFeedbackNpsPrompt re-checks admission/checkedInAt/event.status AND re-checks no feedback row already exists before ever composing the NPS prompt, exactly as REQ-026's existing jobs re-verify their own selection predicates at send time).

7. apps/bot/src/handlers/feedback.ts (NEW): advanceFeedbackFlow (Sec6.4 -- sends the next prompt or the completion notice, called from every write path below regardless of whether that path's own gate wrote anything, so a stale tap/reply never dead-ends silently); makeFeedbackNpsCallbackHandler (Sec6.1 -- extracts nps/registrationId, defensive isValidNpsValue check, resolves flowUser, S3 ownership check BEFORE any write [context.userId !== flowUser.id refuses with notYourFeedback, show_alert], derives FeedbackFlowStep fresh, writes writeFeedbackNps only when step.kind==='feedback-field' && step.field==='nps'); makeFeedbackBroadcastCallbackHandler (Sec6.2 -- identical ownership-then-derive-then-gate shape; AC5's 'does not ask again' is structural: a stale re-tap re-derives step.kind==='complete', never 'broadcast-ask' again, so the gate fails and nothing is written); makeFeedbackTextReplyHandler (Sec6.3 -- the generic reply-to-message listener implementing THE FIX this design's rework was about: step 8's field-match gate checks step.field !== parsed.field in addition to the pre-existing nps/kind checks, so a stale reply to an OLDER, already-superseded prompt for one field is a no-op even when a DIFFERENT sibling field is now the currently-expected one, rather than being silently misattributed to the wrong column).

8. apps/bot/src/i18n/{types.ts,en.ts,ru.ts}: added the feedback top-level catalog key (Sec7) -- npsPrompt, reminderPrefix, likedPrompt/improvePrompt/topicVotesPrompt, skipButton, broadcastAskPrompt/broadcastYesLabel/broadcastNoLabel, completedNotice, staleMessage, notYourFeedback, refLinePrefix/fieldLinePrefix (both fixed literal 'Feedback ref: '/'Feedback field: ' values in both locales, listed only so catalogs.test.ts's parity check keeps enforcing their presence -- never actually looked up through the per-language catalog by domain/feedback.ts's own FEEDBACK_REF_LINE_PREFIX/FEEDBACK_FIELD_LINE_PREFIX constants, which are hardcoded, matching REQ-030 Sec7.1's identical treatment of its own fixed prefixes). Placeholder/minimal functional copy per decisions/0002 (CONTENT-BA owns final wording).

9. apps/bot/src/index.ts: registered makeFeedbackRequestJob/makeFeedbackReminderJob in startScheduledJobs (Sec5.7, same 300000ms interval as every other scheduled job), plus the two new callback patterns (FEEDBACK_NPS_PATTERN, FEEDBACK_BROADCAST_PATTERN) and the generic message:text listener (makeFeedbackTextReplyHandler), placed after every bot.command(...) registration alongside the other generic message:text listener (handlers/profile.ts's makeProfileTextAnswerHandler), matching that file's own established ordering discipline -- both listeners independently no-op on a message they do not recognize, no explicit next() is called by either.

Did NOT touch staff.ts (ISS-0020, explicitly out of scope). No no_show/waitlist-position/seats-taken/registration_open/finished-shaped column was added -- this requirement's only schema additions are the feedback table and users.broadcast_opt_in_asked_at, both named explicitly in the approved schema artefact. No Talk entity or 'want to speak' question anywhere in this diff (AC6).

Verification: `npm run lint -w apps/bot` -> exit 0, zero problems. `npm run build -w apps/bot` -> exit 0, tsc clean. Applied the generated migration to the scratch Postgres (docker container bot-postgres-1, port 55432) via `DATABASE_URL=... npx drizzle-kit migrate` -- succeeded. Ran the FULL existing test suite with `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, no path filter): 31 files / 308 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- identical pass count to the pre-existing baseline (re-verified by stashing this diff and re-running against 18f176c: same 308/308 with --no-file-parallelism), confirming zero regressions. Note on test-runner flakiness: `npm test` (plain `vitest run`, default file-level parallelism) intermittently fails a large fraction of the DB-backed suite with 'deadlock detected'/FK-violation errors from concurrent TRUNCATE calls racing across test files that share one scratch Postgres connection pool -- this reproduces identically at the pre-existing merge-base (18f176c) with none of this run's changes applied, so it is structurally pre-existing test-infrastructure flakiness, not a regression introduced here (Failure Attribution route 2: reproduces at the merge-base, exact output shown in this run's own transcript). Filed as a finding below per core-directives' No Issue Left Local-Only rather than fixed here (out of this run's scope: apps/bot/docker-compose.yml and the test files' own beforeEach/afterEach TRUNCATE calls belong to a different, already-closed requirement).

Direct DB-level invariant verification beyond the regression suite (no TEST-DESIGNER pass has run yet for this requirement -- that is Step 3, after REVIEWER): ran a scripted transaction directly against the migrated scratch Postgres seeding a real chapter/venue/event/user/registration, then (a) inserted a feedback row (nps=8) successfully, (b) attempted a second INSERT for the same registration_id and confirmed Postgres raised unique_violation (AC2's own stated verification method, a raw duplicate INSERT bypassing the application layer entirely), and (c) attempted an out-of-range nps=11 insert and confirmed check_violation from chk_feedback_nps_range -- transaction rolled back afterward, no residual rows.

`git status --porcelain` confirms exactly the files listed in artifacts_out plus the untracked migration/snapshot pair -- no stray file, apps/web and messages/** untouched, staff.ts untouched.

commands: npx drizzle-kit generate (apps/bot) -> generated drizzle/0006_smiling_leader.sql; re-run after schema.ts edits -> 'No schema changes, nothing to migrate'
npm run lint -w apps/bot (repo root) -> exit 0, zero problems
npm run build -w apps/bot (repo root) -> exit 0, tsc clean
npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root, full suite, this diff applied) -> 31 files / 308 tests passed, 0 failed
git stash; npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root, merge-base 18f176c) -> 31 files / 308 tests passed, 0 failed (baseline confirmed identical); git stash pop restored this diff

npm test (plain `vitest run`, default parallelism) on this diff -> 104 failed / 204 passed, all failures 'deadlock detected' or FK-violation from concurrent TRUNCATE; re-ran the SAME command at merge-base 18f176c (diff stashed) -> 101 failed / 207 passed, same failure signature -- confirms pre-existing, not a regression
docker exec bot-postgres-1 psql -U bot -d bot -c "\d feedback" -> table/columns/indexes/constraints match REQ-031-schema.md Sec2 exactly

docker exec bot-postgres-1 psql ... scripted DO block: real chapter/venue/event/user/registration seeded, feedback INSERT (nps=8) succeeds, duplicate INSERT for the same registration_id raises unique_violation (AC2), nps=11 INSERT raises check_violation (chk_feedback_nps_range) -- all inside one transaction, ROLLBACK at the end

ac_results.AC1: Structurally satisfied -- selectRegistrationsForFeedbackRequest's checked_in_at IS NOT NULL clause is the entire mechanism (an admitted-but-never-checked-in registration is excluded by construction), re-verified defensively at compose time via getRegistrationFeedbackContext. Not yet exercised by an automated test (TEST-DESIGNER's job, Step 3) -- code-reading + design-mapping verification only at this step.
ac_results.AC2: PASS, verified directly against the live scratch Postgres: a genuine duplicate INSERT into feedback for the same registration_id raises 23505 unique_violation, independent of any application code (the AC's own stated verification method)
ac_results.AC3: Structurally satisfied -- nps NOT NULL means no row can exist without it (writeFeedbackNps is the sole INSERT path); the three *_skipped columns plus determineNextFeedbackField's ordering give the durable skip/resolved distinction. Not yet exercised end-to-end by an automated test.
ac_results.AC4: Structurally satisfied -- feedback_request/feedback_reminder are distinct NotificationKinds, each independently governed by notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) constraint (REQ-025, unchanged); selectRegistrationsForFeedbackReminder additionally excludes anyone with an existing feedback row. Not yet exercised end-to-end by an automated test.
ac_results.AC5: Structurally satisfied -- determineFeedbackFlowStep gates the broadcast-ask on broadcastOptInAskedAt !== null (never on the boolean answer), a global per-user column read identically regardless of which registration's flow is asking. Not yet exercised end-to-end by an automated test.
ac_results.AC6: PASS by construction -- grep confirms no 'talks'/'Talk' identifier anywhere in this diff's schema, domain, handler, or scheduler files; no speaker-related prompt/callback/catalog key exists
ac_results.AC7: PASS by construction -- both feedback jobs call sendLedgeredNotification with classification:'transactional', and sendLedgeredNotification's own code path (domain/notification.ts, unchanged) never reads broadcastOptIn for a transactional send

issues.title: Plain `vitest run` (npm test) is unsafe against the shared scratch Postgres -- concurrent file-level parallelism races TRUNCATE across DB-backed test files
issues.description: `npm test` (repo root) runs Vitest with default file-level parallelism against one shared scratch Postgres connection pool (localhost:55432). Multiple *.db.test.ts/*.forgery.test.ts files each run their own beforeEach/afterEach TRUNCATE against overlapping tables concurrently, producing intermittent 'deadlock detected' and foreign-key-violation errors unrelated to any specific requirement's logic. Reproduces identically at merge-base 18f176c with zero WF02-REQ-031 changes applied (101 failed/207 passed) and on this branch (104 failed/204 passed) -- same failure signature both times. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` is unaffected (308/308 passing on both). This is pre-existing test-infrastructure flakiness, not attributable to this run.
